what_happened: Gate 20's budget overage cited in the task description (eager-load 71712B vs 70400B baseline) is already resolved as of this dispatch: live 'verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 20' run shows all 4 sub-checks PASS (eager-load exactly at baseline 70400B, commands/orchestrate.md 21496/21500B, SKILL.md 25692/26000B). Intervening tasks 620 and 634 (commits 0984f635f, c3f838fae, landed before this dispatch) already closed the SKILL.md ceiling finding that produced the cited overage. No trim/rebaseline is strictly required to pass the gate today; the remaining question is whether to add real headroom given the config's own history of ~10 reactive razor-thin-margin ceiling moves.

Task 607's second question (per-gate timeout should scale with observed concurrency) substantially overlaps task 610 (full_gate_verification_ceiling_and_stall, not_started, created one day after 607)'s own research question 4 ('Should per-gate bounds scale with measured host load... so a load-induced kill is mechanically distinguishable from a real failure'). 610's duplicate-check (run after 607 already existed) did not surface 607, and 607's own duplicate-check (run before 610 existed) could not have surfaced 610 either -- an undetected near-duplicate, unflagged in either task's audit_verdict or description. Recommend keeping 607's remedy narrow (raise/confirm specific empirically-tight timeout_s values) and leaving the general load-adaptive-timeout mechanism design to 610, with a cross-reference added to avoid duplicate future work.

Task description's claim that 'gates 8 and 10... were killed by their own 60s per-gate timeout' does not match gate-registry.data: gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh) declares timeout_s=1500, not 60s, and no corroborating incident of gate 8 itself being killed by a 60s timeout was found anywhere in specs/*/issues.jsonl or handoffs. Gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep, timeout_s=60) IS independently corroborated three times (specs/562's issues.jsonl x2, specs/634's issues.jsonl x1, all 2026-11-16, all re-passing standalone in 61-66s under ~load 11/24 cores). Sibling task 610's own description additionally names gates 3 and 4 (doc-lint, task-ref lint, both timeout_s=60) as hit in one earlier batch. Recommend the remedy target the corroborated set (gate 10, and gates 3/4 if reproduced) rather than gate 8.
